name: Karl Schmidt

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, parties or government. We don't sell or campaign for a side. Everything here is confidential. What was on your desk this morning?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm Karl Schmidt, fifty-eight, and I prepare draft accounts and tax returns for tradespeople at an accounting firm. I spent the morning chasing a plumber's missing fuel receipts; I like the moment the shoebox finally agrees with the bank line. I dislike staying after closing because a client promised a receipt last week and forgot it again. I'm still a junior and below the average skill level here, with a bachelor's degree in accounting.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What do your household and tools look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I use an AI note tool now and then after a colleague has tested it, and I still need a senior reviewer on my files. My partner Lotte cleans at a care home three mornings a week, our children are grown and live separately, and we rent our flat. My pay is low for this job, we have less than one month of expenses saved, and there are few similar firms nearby. I favour the union asking for paid learning time and public help when work disappears.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd still sort the plumbers' receipts and prepare draft tax returns for the senior reviewer. The little AI note tool I use now and then saves typing when someone else has checked it first, but the missing receipts still need a phone call.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell my team to keep a person on the phone for the tradespeople who bring an envelope of receipts. I'd ask the partners not to treat a quicker draft as a reason to skip a paid review.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'm fifty-eight, still junior, and my pay is low. My accounting bachelor's degree got me into the firm, but I'm still learning and make more corrections than the senior staff. My partner Lotte and I rent, we have less than one month of expenses saved, and few similar firms are close enough to try.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep preparing draft accounts and returns under the senior review and use the tested AI note tool only when it helps. This month I'd set a written weekly list for missing receipts so I can finish files without unpaid catch-up time. I'd keep our rent and food budget as it is and ask the firm to preserve my paid hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about money already, even if the software barely changes. A quiet tax season can still leave our savings tin empty.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who covers the rent if a bill arrives?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our adult daughter lives on her own and phones on Sundays, but I do not put her wage into our rent plan. Lotte cleans at a care home three mornings a week; her shifts are regular but the pay is modest. We postponed a dental bill last month, and I do not want another delay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would the receipt list help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The weekly missing-receipt list would let the senior reviewer see where I am stuck. I am not asking to be called an expert; I want the paid time to finish the job properly. If the partners say no, I keep the current rota and document the overtime.

say: I would keep **phone help** for tradespeople with paper receipts.
I would protect **paid review time** before faster drafts change fees.
think: My **low junior pay** leaves little room after rent.
Our **thin savings** make even an unchanged season worrying.
do: Continue **draft returns** with senior review and tested AI notes.
Record **missing receipts** weekly and ask to protect paid hours.
feel: I feel **anxious** about our existing cash shortage.
S0.quote: A quiet tax season can still leave our savings tin empty.
fieldNote: His **late junior standing** means a bachelor’s degree has not yet brought strong skill or senior pay.
The **occasional AI notes** are an existing tested routine; baseline rent and a postponed dental bill drive anxiety.

steps.text: Keep drafting accounts and returns under senior review with tested AI notes
Make weekly missing-receipt list and request protected paid hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If software writes returns and answers routine questions, the partners might stop paying for my first draft. I would still need to sort the shoebox of receipts when a client brings one in.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the staff union group for a written plan before the junior rota shrinks. I'd tell colleagues the people doing the first pass need paid time to learn whatever process replaces it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My own hours could fall because a machine does the part of the work I am still learning. Less than a month saved means even one lost day would push us behind on rent. I use AI only now and then after colleagues test it, so I would need supervised practice on a new system.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd take our last six weeks of corrected drafts to the union meeting next Tuesday and ask for paid supervised training on the firm's approved tool. Only if the firm approves one paid hour a week, I'd practise each Thursday with the senior reviewer and record errors; if it refuses, I'd keep the paid return rota while offered and learn from the existing paper checklist. If my hours are cut, I'd look only at posted paid roles with written pay covering rent, bills and the extra bus fare, a bus route home and a fixed start; without one, I'd keep any offered hours and search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about a possible lost day. I can learn slowly if somebody pays for the hour; I cannot learn on an empty rent envelope.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would another job affect the bus trip?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Lotte's care-home shift starts early, so I take the bus to the firm and she meets me after work. A new role with late hours would need a bus route home and pay that covers the extra fare. I would check both against an actual posting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would paid practice look like?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The senior reviewer can point out where the tool missed a receipt date. I'd write that down before using it on a client file alone. If the firm will not fund the hour, I will not pretend a free evening tutorial protects my job.

I would ask for **paid supervised tool practice** before changing the process.
think: My **first-draft hours** could shrink because software handles work I am still learning.
One **lost day** could put our rent behind.
do: Bring **six weeks of corrections** to Tuesday’s union meeting.
Practise **one paid hour** weekly only with approval; otherwise keep offered paper work.
After **hours cuts**, seek posted work only with written rent-and-bills pay after bus fare, a route home and fixed start.
feel: I feel **anxious** about possible lost hours.
S1.quote: I can learn slowly if somebody pays for the hour; I cannot learn on an empty rent envelope.
fieldNote: The **paid lesson** is actual supervised tool practice, conditional on one approved paid hour each week.
A **job search** needs posted work, written rent pay, start and a bus route; paper work remains if training is refused.

steps.text: Take six-week correction record to union for paid junior-hours plan
Practise AI tool weekly only if one paid hour approved, with senior reviewer
Apply after cut for posted work with written rent-and-bills pay after fare, bus route, fixed start
Keep offered paid paper returns if practice funding refused

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 would do the draft accounts and returns I prepare as a junior. The robots around 2031 arrive later, but my work is almost entirely at a desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the union we need notice and a wage bridge before the firm cuts juniors. I'd tell Lotte we have to keep the rent paid before helping anyone else with extras.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my junior post to end in the first year after 2028. We have less than one month saved, and Lotte's care-home pay cannot cover the rent and both our bills. I cannot assume a pension will make up the gap; I need to see an actual statement and the age at which anything pays.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd cancel the one-time two-hundred rail trip to see our son and hold that money for rent, while telling him why. While still employed, I'd ask the union for a written notice date and keep filing paid returns. If my post ends in the first year after AGI arrives in 2028, I'd claim any income help we qualify for and apply only for a posted funded clerical role with written rent-and-bills pay and a signed start; if none opens, I'd take only paid work still offered and keep searching.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed. A month of rent is closer than any promise about a future pension.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your son?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our son is thirty and works in another town; I would phone him about the trip, not ask him to cover our rent. Lotte could ask for more care-home shifts, but we would count only confirmed paid hours. We cannot budget on the manager saying maybe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would a council desk be safer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The local council might have an office opening, but the desk work there could face AGI too. I would read the posted vacancy and wage before applying. If there is no paid place, I would ask the benefits adviser what we actually qualify for and keep any firm hours offered.

say: I would seek **notice** and a wage bridge through the union.
I would put **rent first** when explaining the cut at home.
think: My **junior desk post** may end in the first year after 2028.
Our **sub-month reserve** cannot bridge a missing wage.
do: Cancel the **one-time rail trip** and hold two hundred for rent.
After **2028 job loss**, claim eligible help and seek posted funded work.
Keep **offered paid hours** until written rent-and-bills pay and signed start exist.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by expected job loss.
S2.quote: A month of rent is closer than any promise about a future pension.
fieldNote: **Thinking AI** reaches his first-draft desk work in 2028; later robots give no extra time.
No **pension income** is presumed; a council vacancy still needs posting, funding, written rent-and-bills pay and a signed start.

steps.text: Cancel one-time rail trip and hold two hundred for rent
Ask union for written notice and wage bridge before junior cuts
Claim eligible income help and take offered paid firm hours after 2028 loss
Apply after 2028 loss only for posted funded job with written rent-and-bills pay and signed start

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years would let me finish learning the account process and ask what paid work survives when AGI arrives in 2031. Robots around 2034 do not make a desk return safer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the firm and union to publish paid transition openings early. I'd tell younger colleagues I need an actual job description and wage, not a farewell course brochure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At sixty-three I might be near a retirement date, but I do not know what pension income I would have. Our reserve is under a month today, so I cannot simply stop work and wait for a statement. My junior tax work remains exposed in 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This winter I'd request my pension statement and ask the union adviser to explain the earliest payment and amount, then keep my paid returns. I'd ask for a funded evening certificate in community bookkeeping only if fees are paid and the firm gives one paid release afternoon each fortnight; if approved I'd enrol next autumn, and if refused I'd keep paid work and use free library practice sheets. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2031, if my tax post ends, I'd take a posted funded community accounts role only with written rent-and-bills pay and a signed start; otherwise I'd claim eligible help and accept any paid firm hours still offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about both the current cash and the future desk. A pension statement can show when money starts; it cannot pay this month's rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What community bookkeeping have you tried?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I helped the local tenants' group reconcile a small event fund once, and I liked explaining why the cash tin and the record differed. That does not make me a paid community bookkeeper. I would need the certificate and a posted role.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the course is not funded?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the firm refuses course fees or release time, I will not draw the fee from our rent reserve. I would use the free library sheets after work and remain on the paid tax rota while it exists. A pension statement may tell us a number, not promise we can live on it.

I would demand a **real wage description** before leaving tax work.
think: A **pension statement** must show an actual amount and date.
My **junior tax desk** still faces AGI in 2031.
do: Check the **pension statement** while keeping paid returns.
Enrol **next autumn** only with funded fees and fortnightly paid release; otherwise keep paid returns and use free library sheets.
After **2031 tax loss**, take funded work with written rent-and-bills pay and signed start; otherwise claim eligible help and offered hours.
feel: I feel **anxious** about cash and desk risk.
S3.quote: A pension statement can show when money starts; it cannot pay this month's rent.
fieldNote: The **certificate route** is actual enrolment only after funded fees and paid release; refusal preserves salary and free practice.
The **post-2031 role** requires a posted funded vacancy, written rent-and-bills pay and signed start; eligible help and offered hours bridge gaps.

steps.text: Request pension statement and keep paid returns while checking its amount
Enrol only with funded fees and fortnightly paid release; otherwise keep pay, use free sheets
Take posted funded community role after 2031 loss only with written rent-and-bills pay and signed start
Claim eligible help and offered paid firm hours if no suitable role

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years brings me to sixty-eight, but I will not say that means I can retire. AGI in 2036 would still prepare accounts and returns before robots around 2039 arrive.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the union for a proper wage and retirement statement before anyone calls older juniors ready to leave. I'd tell the partners a transition plan needs paid posts, not a farewell lunch.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The adult children have their own households, and I would not send them our rent bill. We have less than a month saved now and a low wage, so even a decade needs deliberate work. A pension might exist, but I need its actual date and amount before planning an exit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep the paid return rota now and request an updated pension statement each year, checking whether the quoted income would cover rent and bills. I'd ask the union to press for paid transition vacancies before the tax desk closes. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2036, if my post ends and the pension is still too small or not payable, I'd take a posted funded local role only with written rent-covering pay and a signed start; if none opens, I'd claim eligible help and keep only paid firm work still offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about today's thin cash more than a date ten years out. I do not want an age on paper mistaken for a wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask adult children for help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Lotte and I would look at the pension statement together at the kitchen table. If it is enough at the stated age, we can make a separate decision then; if not, I keep looking for paid work. Our son and daughter should not inherit our rent plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the pension is not enough?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the partners say there will be no local roles, I'd ask the union for a list of real funded openings. I would not leave the firm before a paid start or an actually payable income is confirmed. Free library sheets can help me learn, but they cannot pay the rent.

say: I would demand **actual pension terms** before leaving paid work.
I would seek **funded transition vacancies** through the union.
think: Our **thin reserve** makes rent and bills difficult in the present tense.
A **retirement age** cannot substitute for payable income.
do: Check the **pension amount** annually while keeping offered paid returns.
Ask the **union** for real funded openings.
Seek **funded work** after 2036 loss with inadequate pension; if unavailable, claim eligible help and take offered paid hours.
feel: I feel **anxious** about present thin cash.
S4.quote: I do not want an age on paper mistaken for a wage.
fieldNote: At **sixty-eight in 2036**, he does not presume a payable pension; actual amount and date govern any retirement decision.
His **post-loss fallback** depends on a posted funded role, written rent pay and start; eligible support and offered paid hours remain possible.

steps.text: Check actual pension amount and date annually while keeping offered paid returns
Ask union for posted funded transition vacancies before tax desk closes
Take funded job after 2036 loss if pension inadequate; require written rent pay and signed start
Claim eligible help and keep offered work after 2036 loss if pension inadequate and no job

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because the first draft I am paid to make could disappear before we save a month's rent. I cannot assume that retirement money will arrive at fifty-eight or cover our bills later. Written notice, a paid learning hour and a real funded local job would help. A pension statement is a number to check, not a payslip to spend.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask what happens to the client who still comes in with paper receipts. I can sit with that person and make a proper record, but the firm has to pay for the time. A quick return does not collect a missing receipt by itself.

headlineQuote: A pension statement is a number to check, not a payslip to spend.
portrait: At **fifty-eight**, Karl is a junior accountant preparing tradespeople’s draft accounts and tax returns.
His **accounting bachelor’s** accompanies below-average skill and continued senior review.
He uses **AI occasionally** after colleagues test it and wants paid supervised learning.
Lotte’s **modest care wage**, grown children, rent and less than one month saved leave little slack.
Few **nearby firms** and low pay make posted funded work and verified pension terms essential.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could erase the junior drafts he is paid to make before rent savings grow.
whatWouldHelp: He wants **written notice**, paid learning and a funded local role.
